source: PVII_mother_tree_v4_levers_review.xlsx (literature review of the v4 levers, uploaded 10 November 2026), Codebook sheet
rule: A lever is dropped when the review grades the whole lever unbacked (column 'backing grade (review)'), i.e. after the review's corrections and proposed sources it still scores below 1.5: no framework support and at most thin evidence on the action itself. Levers the review grades unbacked for only one part (LV-010, LV-195, LV-222) or that 'could fall' to unbacked (LV-223) are kept.

dropped.lever: Food safety standards, inspection, certification and traceability
dropped.review_justified_by: Hoffmann et al. 2019 (#375); Havelaar et al. 2015 (#760); Jaffee et al. 2019 (#783). No confirmed systematic review of inspection or traceability in LMICs.
dropped.review_comment: The lever is a real policy area with a thin evidence base. The Thai list mixes food safety control with organic and farm certification, which is a market-value action, and with export standards. Say so in the test.

dropped.lever: Storage, cold chains and post-harvest handling
dropped.review_justified_by: Omotilewa et al. 2018 (#434); Affognon et al. 2015 (#524); proposed Basu and Wong 2015 (10.1016/j.jdeveco.2015.02.001), Sheahan and Barrett 2017 (10.1016/j.foodpol.2017.03.012).
dropped.review_comment: Keep as a lever; the evidence is thin and African. The boundary with strategic food stocks is missing: a public grain warehouse is a stock (LV-175), a farm silo is post-harvest handling.

dropped.lever: Legal aid, alternative dispute resolution, access to justice
dropped.review_justified_by: Blattman, Hartman and Blair 2014 (#598); Sandefur and Siddiqi 2013 (#899); Anda et al. 2022 (#264); Chemin 2009 (moves to LV-166). Proposed: Maru 2009 (10.1596/18102).
dropped.review_comment: Weak evidence base. The one double-coded case shows the test admits environmental disputes, which belong to a natural-resources family. Keep the lever but narrow it to people's access to legal help and community dispute resolution.

dropped.lever: Digital skills training for workers, students and firms
dropped.review_justified_by: Novella et al. 2026 (#430); Akerman et al. 2015 (#531); Aker et al. 2012 proposed (10.1257/app.4.4.94, partial fit).
dropped.review_comment: Evidence is thin, so this lever should not take general digital lines. Say that a school digital curriculum is LV-053 and English or general skills courses are LV-059. The unclear pilot-programme title needs a rule: it goes here only if it teaches digital skills.

dropped.lever: Biosecurity and invasive species control
dropped.review_justified_by: Part A #384 (partial), #877; Keller, Lodge and Finnoff 2007 PNAS 10.1073/pnas.0605787104 (screening benefits, model-based); Diagne et al 2021 Nature 10.1038/s41586-021-03405-6 (cost of invasions; metadata only)
dropped.review_comment: The only evidence is island eradication, and agricultural biosecurity belongs to LV-153. Rewrite as an ecological lever (invasive species and wildlife-harming biosecurity) and exclude pests and diseases of crops and livestock. No Thai strategy or framework supports it; leave unbacked.

dropped.lever: Disclosure and management of guarantees, SOE and PPP liabilities
dropped.family: Public wealth: resource rents and the balance sheet
dropped.review_justified_by: Part A #295, #603; no intervention evidence read
dropped.review_comment: Keep, with a better exclusion (PPP contracts are LV-206). The evidence documents the size of the risk, not what disclosure does, so it stays unbacked. The one Thai line fits.

dropped.lever: Long-term fiscal planning for ageing and future generations
dropped.family: Public wealth: resource rents and the balance sheet
dropped.review_justified_by: Part A #429 (none), #557 fix citation
dropped.review_comment: As worded the lever is a motive, not an action. Rewrite it around an instrument (long-run fiscal projections, generational accounts, ageing-cost reports) so it can be tested. No intervention evidence exists; it stays unbacked.

dropped.lever: Retirement age, incentives and support for older workers
dropped.review_justified_by: Part A #461, #743; Mastrobuoni 2009 J Public Econ 10.1016/j.jpubeco.2009.07.009 and Seibold 2021 AER 10.1257/aer.20191136 candidate
dropped.review_comment: Keep. The Thai lines are employment support for older people, not retirement-age rules; the evidence from Austria covers the latter. Evidence is thin but direct.

dropped.lever: Long-term care systems, financing and family caregiver support
dropped.review_comment: Add residential and community care to the joins-when so facility strategies do not drift to the family level (s179). Evidence is a single Japanese quasi-experiment.

dropped.lever: Air routes and connectivity for business travel
dropped.review_justified_by: Campante and Yanagizawa-Drott 2018 (#308, #614 same paper, dedupe); Giroud 2013; Blonigen and Cristea 2015 (10.1016/j.jue.2015.02.001).
dropped.review_comment: Mechanism is sound but empty in the Thai set. The exclusion of tourism arrivals leaves them without a home unless NEW-EXP-1 is added.

dropped.lever: Destination development, secondary destinations
dropped.backing_grade_review: unbacked (0.5); unchanged with Brida 2016 and Lonn 2018, which are mechanism or case evidence
dropped.review_justified_by: Faber and Gaubert 2019 (Part A #346 partial, #707 direct fix citation; local spillovers, national offset); Brida et al. 2016 (10.1080/13683500.2013.868414, mechanism review); Lonn et al. 2018 (10.1016/j.ecolecon.2018.04.036, community tourism income small). Joins-not rewritten to point to levers.
dropped.review_comment: The lever is a sound cut, but its evidence is a single Mexican study of local spillovers and one negative Cambodian case. Rewrite the joins-not to point to sibling levers. Check that medical and wellness strategies belong here or in LV-133/134, and that regulation of destination investment (s81) is admitted. Keep the unbacked grade.

dropped.lever: Carrying-capacity rules, sustainable tourism management and site
dropped.review_justified_by: Butler 1980 (Part A #611, fit direct, no tests); Ekin et al. 2026 (#342, partial narrative review); Capocchi et al. 2019 (10.3390/su11123303); Andam et al. 2010 (10.1073/pnas.0914177107, Thai site protection, partial).
dropped.review_comment: The lever is clear and Thai strategies use it. The name was cut off at 'site'; the full phrase fits in 64 characters. Evidence is conceptual only, so leave it unbacked. Sort mixed 'grow and protect' strategies by main aim and check the destination-development strategies in the Thai set.

dropped.lever: Diversification of source markets and tourism crisis measures
dropped.review_justified_by: Gossling, Scott and Hall 2021 (Part A #736, partial, descriptive); Rossello et al. 2020 (10.1016/j.tourman.2020.104080, disasters reduce arrivals; recovery time not measured). No source tests diversification itself.
dropped.review_comment: The lever is defensible but empty in the Thai set and without intervention evidence. Rename not needed; the joins-not now points to sibling levers. Decide whether to keep an empty lever or fold it into LV-108 as a single 'tourism risk' lever.

dropped.lever: Diaspora engagement for trade, investment and knowledge
dropped.review_comment: Mechanism is credible with three network studies; programme evidence is missing. The overlap with LV-162 is the key test.

dropped.lever: Reskilling and support for workers displaced by automation
dropped.review_justified_by: Part A rows 380 Jacobson et al partial, 518 Acemoglu and Restrepo direct; proposals Dauth et al 2021 (10.1093/jeea/jvab012), Hyman, Kovak and Leive 2024 (10.3386/w32464).
dropped.review_comment: Agree with the flag: drop the technology-direction clause, which no attached source tests. What remains is reskilling displaced workers, which Jacobson et al show but not specific to automation. If the economists want technology-origin to matter, keep it; if not, merge with LV-159 as a lever for displaced workers.

dropped.lever: Forecasting, early-warning systems and hazard monitoring
dropped.review_justified_by: Burlig et al. 2024 (Part A #306), Hallegatte 2012 (#748); Bakkensen and Mendelsohn 2016 10.1086/685908 proposed
dropped.review_comment: Keep. Replace pathway codes in the joins-not with lever ids. Say that hazard and risk modelling for warnings belongs here, not in the registry lever. Evidence is one Indian RCT plus a policy paper; there is no systematic review of early-warning effectiveness.

dropped.lever: Disease surveillance, laboratories and outbreak response
dropped.review_justified_by: Phalkey et al. 2015 (#439); Heymann and Rodier 2004 citation to fix (#765)
dropped.review_comment: Keep; swap pathway ids for lever ids. Tie-break with LV-172: if the strategy is aimed at the animal-human source, LV-172; if it detects cases in people, here. Evidence is descriptive; no Asian outcome study found.

dropped.lever: One Health programmes at the animal-human-environment interface
dropped.review_justified_by: Baum et al. 2017 (#281), Jones et al. 2008 (#792)
dropped.review_comment: Keep with lever-id joins-not. Honest note: only seven of 1,839 One Health papers reported quantitative outcomes, so the grade should stay unbacked. Mixed surveillance-and-source programmes need a tie-break: whichever is named first.

dropped.lever: Reducing concentration and dependence in trade and supply
dropped.review_justified_by: Carvalho et al. 2021 10.1093/qje/qjaa044 and Barrot and Sauvagnat 2016 10.1093/qje/qjw018 (L3-202); Cavalcanti et al. 2015 (#623), Deaton 1999 (#664) (L3-199); Farrell and Newman 2019 (#710) (L3-203); Volpe Martincus and Carballo 2008 (#470) is only partial
dropped.review_comment: Split into two. One lever for supplier diversification and chokepoint security, one for export and commodity diversification. Remove the self-referencing joins-not. The attached export-promotion papers do not test lower dependence; replace with exposure evidence and state that no intervention evidence exists.

dropped.lever: Foresight, scenarios and long-term strategy units
dropped.review_justified_by: School of International Futures 2021 (#456), Schwartz 1991 (#901), Wack 1985 (#925, fix citation); Habegger 2010 proposed
dropped.review_comment: Keep, using lever ids. Be plain that the evidence is practitioner and case-based; no foresight evaluation from Asia or middle-income governments was found. Firm studies (Rohrbeck and Kum) are only an analogy.

dropped.lever: National, sector and investment plans that coordinate investment
dropped.review_justified_by: Lane 2025 (#400), Murphy et al. 1989 (#852), Rosenstein-Rodan 1943 (#895)
dropped.review_comment: Agree with the fix, and say the evidence covers only coordinated sector drives. Of the six Thai strategies, the health crisis plan belongs in LV-197 and the energy R&D planning item in an R&D lever. No causal evidence that national plans as such raise outcomes, which should be stated.

dropped.lever: Statistical systems, surveys, censuses and analysis for decisions
dropped.review_justified_by: Hjort et al. 2021 (#374), Jerven 2013 (#791), Devarajan 2013 (#668); Sandefur and Glassman 2015 10.1080/00220388.2014.968138 proposed
dropped.review_comment: Keep with lever ids. Dashboard cases need a rule: analysis for planning is here, tracking a programme's own performance is in LV-182. Evidence is about data quality and information use, not causal effects of statistical capacity; no systematic review found.

dropped.lever: Shared registries, data standards
dropped.review_justified_by: Leite et al. 2017 (#405), OECD 2019 (#863, drop the 'still to check' tag); World Bank 2022 10.1596/38520 proposed
dropped.review_comment: Keep. Lever ids in the tests, and a tie-break for strategies that both digitise and integrate. The name now fits within 70 characters and is not cut off. Evidence is descriptive: registries as gateways, not shown to improve targeting.

dropped.lever: Iterative, problem-driven reform methods
dropped.review_justified_by: Part A keeps #398, #548, #880. Add Andrews et al. 2013 (10.1016/j.worlddev.2013.05.011) and Rasul and Rogger 2018. #398 is priority tracking, which belongs closer to LV-182 or LV-190.
dropped.review_comment: Two ideas are bundled and the bundle is hard to place: iterative methods (PDCA, design thinking) and sequencing reform to capacity. The joins-not points to this lever's own pathways, so it excludes itself in effect. I would keep one lever but fix the tests and move delivery units explicitly to LV-190 as centre-of-government.

dropped.lever: Cybersecurity standards, agencies and incident response
dropped.review_justified_by: Part A keeps #323, #546. Romanosky 2011 (10.1002/pam.20567) is partly relevant (incident notification).
dropped.review_comment: Keep as a policy-area lever, and say clearly it is unbacked: cyber regulation has not been evaluated in middle-income settings. One tension: 'Government Computer Security Incident Co-ordination Center' is both coordination and cyber; the cyber lever should take it.

dropped.lever: Platform competition and digital market rules
dropped.review_justified_by: Part A keeps #256, #650. Nothing to add (searched).
dropped.review_comment: Keep, but flag it as unbacked and as an EU-based evidence base with zero Thai strategies. Spell out in the joins-not that general competition law goes to LV-164 by id.

dropped.lever: Rules and incentives steering AI and automation
dropped.review_justified_by: Part A keeps #396, #519. Add Acemoglu et al. 2020 on tax bias (10.1353/eca.2020.0003) as mechanism only.
dropped.review_comment: Keep the lever but reword so it covers rules, standards and tax or subsidy incentives for AI and automation, and make clear that a sandbox for AI belongs in LV-184. Evidence is thin and Thai strategies are only two, with no plan-language examples shown.

dropped.lever: Coordinating bodies, integrated mechanisms and whole-of-government
dropped.review_justified_by: Part A keeps #258 and #773 at partial fit. Add Cejudo and Michel 2017 (10.1007/s11077-017-9281-5) for the concept.
dropped.review_comment: The lever is a catch-all (15 Thai strategies) and the double coding shows disagreement on all five cases, so the tests do not sort. I would split it into (a) standing coordinating bodies and whole-of-government centres and (b) local or sector collaboration mechanisms, and add an explicit rule that 'monitoring systems for programmes' goes to LV-182.

dropped.lever: Emergency operations centres, surge staff, beds and stockpiles
dropped.review_justified_by: NASEM 2020 (#426); Neupane et al. 2024; Part A dropped #621
dropped.review_comment: Accept the fix: reserve staff and beds stay here, national stocks go to LV-175. The lever stays unbacked and the tree should say plainly that evidence of effectiveness is absent. The definition needs wording that separates community preparedness (training the public) from agency surge capacity.

dropped.lever: Build-back-better reconstruction
dropped.review_justified_by: Kennedy et al. 2008 (#391); Hallegatte et al. 2018 (replaces #751)
dropped.review_comment: Accept as is but name the evidence honestly: case lessons and modelling, no evaluation. Pointer L3-087 should be LV-070. Zero Thai strategies, so low use.

dropped.lever: Budget preparation, execution and results-based budgeting
dropped.review_justified_by: Vlaicu et al. 2014 (#468), Alesina and Perotti 1996 (#534, fix citation), von Hagen 1992 (#924, fix citation)
dropped.review_comment: Three of three double-coded strategies split across levers. 'Link the plan to the annual budget' sits between this and LV-178. Add a rule: aligning a plan's priorities to the budget goes here; the plan itself goes to LV-178. Pointer L3-097 should be LV-094.
